children: Swiss Life plans to cut around 600 jobs by the end of 2028 in a move to boost efficiency and profitability.

The reduction will take place largely through natural attrition, with about half of the cuts expected in Switzerland and the other half at its asset-management operations abroad, the Zurich-based insurer said Tuesday.
At the end of 2025, Swiss Life had the equivalent of roughly 11,000 full-time positions worldwide and a network of around 17,000 advisors, according to its website.
Swiss Life said it expects around 100 redundancies by the end of this year.
The insurer is halfway through a three-year plan it launched at the end of 2024, and linked the cuts to its goal to expand business profitably beyond 2027.
With the 2027 targets well on track, Swiss Life wants to strengthen its position and efficiency by using digitization to capture market opportunities, Chief Executive Matthias Aellig said.
The company said it is launching a new share buyback of 250 million Swiss francs ($309.3 million), after completing a previous 750 million-franc program in May as planned.
The company had launched the buyback in December 2024 as it set out new targets for higher fee results and return on equity over the 2025-2027 period, among other goals.
For the first half of 2026, Swiss Life said net profit rose to 643 million francs from 585 million francs a year before.
Swiss Life said gross written premiums were up 1.8% to 12.33 billion francs in the first half, helped by 7.1% growth in Switzerland to 6.75 billion francs.
The insurance service result increased to 691 million francs from 659 million francs, while the net investment result grew 14% to 290 million francs.
